subject: anatomy
title: Posterior Mediastinum: Azygos Venous System, Thoracic Duct, and Oesophagus

steps.tx: The posterior mediastinum is located posterior to the pericardium and diaphragm between thoracic vertebral bodies T5 through T12. Its primary longitudinal venous channel is the **azygos vein**, which originates in the abdomen at the confluence of the right subcostal and right ascending lumbar veins.
steps.say: The posterior mediastinum lies behind the heart between vertebrae T5 and T12. Its chief venous channel is the azygos vein, arising in the abdomen from the right subcostal and ascending lumbar veins.

vis.alt: Sagittal anatomy of mediastinum illustrating boundaries of the posterior mediastinum
vis.caption: Posterior mediastinal compartment situated posterior to the pericardium and diaphragm. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Ascending along the right side of the vertebral column through the aortic hiatus, the azygos vein arches anteriorly over the root of the right lung at vertebral level T4. It empties directly into the posterior aspect of the **superior vena cava** immediately before the SVC penetrates the fibrous pericardium.
steps.say: Ascending through the aortic hiatus, the azygos vein arches forward over the right lung root at level T4. It drains into the superior vena cava just before the pericardium.

steps.tx: On the left side of the posterior mediastinum, venous drainage is handled by the hemiazygos and accessory hemiazygos veins. The **hemiazygos vein** ascends on the left from T12 to T9, where it crosses behind the aorta, oesophagus, and thoracic duct to drain into the azygos vein at vertebral level T9.
steps.say: On the left, venous blood is collected by hemiazygos and accessory hemiazygos veins. The hemiazygos vein crosses behind the aorta and oesophagus at T9 to join the azygos vein.

steps.tx: The **thoracic duct** is the largest lymphatic vessel in the body, conveying chyle and lymph from the lower limbs, pelvis, and abdomen. Originating from the cisterna chyli at vertebral level L1/L2, it enters the posterior mediastinum through the aortic hiatus, ascending between the azygos vein and descending aorta.
steps.say: The thoracic duct is the largest lymphatic trunk, conveying lymph from the lower body. Originating from the cisterna chyli, it enters through the aortic hiatus and ascends between aorta and azygos vein.

left.title: Lower Thoracic Course (T12-T5)
points: Enters through aortic hiatus at T12
Ascends on right side of vertebral bodies

right.title: Upper Thoracic Course (T4-Root of Neck)
points: Crosses vertebral column from right to left at T5
Ascends along left border of oesophagus
Arches lateral to left carotid and jugular
Empties into left internal jugular-subclavian junction

steps.tx: Iatrogenic surgical trauma or penetrating injuries to the posterior mediastinum can lacerate the thoracic duct, causing extravasation of milky chyle into the pleural cavity, designated **chylothorax**. Rupture below the T5 crossover produces a right-sided chylothorax, whereas injury above T5 results in a left-sided chylothorax.
steps.say: Surgical trauma to the thoracic duct releases milky chyle into the pleural space, causing chylothorax. Laceration below T5 yields a right-sided chylothorax, while injury above T5 produces a left-sided collection.

steps.tx: The thoracic oesophagus descends vertically through the posterior mediastinum from the lower border of the cricoid cartilage at C6 down to the gastric cardia at T11. Along its twenty-five-centimetre length, the oesophageal lumen exhibits four distinct **anatomical constrictions** where foreign bodies lodge and caustic strictures preferentially develop.
steps.say: The thoracic oesophagus descends twenty-five centimeters from the cricoid cartilage to the stomach. Its lumen has four anatomical constrictions where swallowed foreign bodies lodge.

rows: Arch of aorta crossing left wall

steps.tx: Failure of the lower oesophageal sphincter to relax coupled with aperistalsis produces **achalasia cardia**. On barium swallow radiography, marked dilatation of the proximal oesophagus tapers smoothly to a narrow distal beak, classic for the bird-beak or rat-tail deformity resulting from myenteric plexus degeneration.
steps.say: Failure of the lower oesophageal sphincter to relax causes achalasia cardia. Barium swallow demonstrates marked oesophageal dilatation tapering to a smooth bird-beak deformity.

vis.alt: Barium swallow radiograph demonstrating dilated oesophagus with bird-beak distal narrowing in achalasia
vis.caption: Barium swallow examination demonstrating achalasia cardia with classic bird-beak tapering. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Autonomic motor control to the thoracic viscera is delivered by the **vagus nerve** (CN X). Descending behind the pulmonary roots, the left and right vagi break up into the anterior and posterior pulmonary and oesophageal plexuses, before reforming as anterior and posterior vagal trunks to traverse the diaphragmatic hiatus at T10.
steps.say: The vagus nerves descend behind the lung roots to form pulmonary and oesophageal plexuses. They reorganize into anterior and posterior vagal trunks to cross the diaphragm at T10.

left.title: Anterior Vagal Trunk
points: Formed primarily by left vagus nerve
Travels on anterior surface of oesophagus
Gives hepatic branches and anterior nerve of Latarjet

right.title: Posterior Vagal Trunk
points: Formed primarily by right vagus nerve
Travels on posterior surface of oesophagus
Gives coeliac branches and posterior nerve of Latarjet
Gives criminal nerve of Grassi to gastric fundus
